# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Shokz OpenDots 2 (~$200)**
- WIRED's top pick. Battery is 10 hours (40 with the case), and the IP57 rating survived rain and submersion in their testing.
- The clip-on design leaves the top of your ear free for hats and sunglasses.
- Runner's World also names it best for long runs.
- [WIRED's review and buy links](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best sound: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199, down from $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick. WIRED says they have the clearest sound of the clip-ons and physical buttons that are easier to use mid-run.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new pair within a month, so you may want to wait or watch for clearance deals.
- [Runner's World review and buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (~$180 list, about $125 at REI and Best Buy per WIRED)**
- It keeps your ears the most open, has physical buttons, and lasts 12 hours (IP55).
- Downsides: the neckband can clash with long hair and winter hats, and clarity is a bit below the older OpenRun.
- [WIRED review and buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best value: Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99 at Amazon, down from $149)**
- SoundGuys picks it as best overall open-ear and best for running. It has strong bass for this category, IP54 resistance, and a good app EQ.
- [SoundGuys picks and buy links](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Budget options**
- **JLab Flex Open (~$40-50):** Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to try clip-ons. Sound is less detailed and it has touch controls only. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (~$50):** WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** SoundGuys' budget pick, listed at $79.99 on Amazon. It has an ear hook, IP55, 10 hours per charge, and 42 hours with the case. [Buy via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). Dealectric lists a $129.99 store price and says code AFSC20 takes it to about $104 at Soundcore's store. That conflicts with the Amazon price, so compare before buying.

**How to choose**
- If you want maximum awareness and a locked-in fit, get the OpenRun Pro 2.
- If you want the best sound, get the Bose.
- If you want long battery life and durability, get the OpenDots 2.
- If you're unsure you'll like open-ear, start with the JLab, Soundpeats, or Nothing.

Prices come from the articles and change often. Open-ear buds also leak sound and sound thinner than sealed earbuds, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.
